fit: turmeric exposure and Parkinson pain severity
assessment: Review discusses turmeric-derived curcumin in experimental formulations, including non-dietary applications, without a culinary pain comparison.

fit: orange exposure and Parkinson fall frequency
assessment: Drug-delivery review discusses orange-derived extracellular vesicles as engineered cancer-targeting carriers, not culinary orange or Parkinson outcomes.

fit: cinnamon exposure and Parkinson olfactory impairment severity
assessment: Human olfactory testing uses cinnamon as an odor cue; identification did not distinguish study groups, and ingestion was not tested.

fit: grape exposure and Parkinson muscle rigidity severity
assessment: Grape juice is a biosensor validation matrix. The analytical test does not measure a clinical response after consuming grapes.

fit: ginger exposure and Parkinson pain severity
assessment: This review describes ginger-derived particles in a preclinical colitis context. Culinary ginger and the assigned Parkinson outcome are untested.

fit: ginger exposure and Parkinson anxiety severity
assessment: Depression delivery review describes ginger-derived nanoparticles interacting with gut microbes; no independent culinary ginger treatment outcome is established.

fit: corn oil exposure and Parkinson depressive symptom severity
assessment: Alzheimer mouse study uses corn oil as vehicle for tamoxifen; this does not isolate a dietary corn-oil outcome.

fit: salmon exposure and Parkinson bradykinesia severity
assessment: Review describes salmon-derived DNA in a biomimetic material, not dietary salmon or a Parkinson motor comparison.

fit: sunflower oil exposure and Parkinson muscle rigidity severity
assessment: Parkinson-model rats receive sunflower oil as injectable vehicle; coordination and exploration were assessed, not oil-only rigidity.

fit: turmeric exposure and Parkinson fall frequency
assessment: Cell-death review describes curcumin as a turmeric constituent; Agent Orange denotes a herbicide, not orange fruit.

fit: millet exposure and Parkinson pain severity
assessment: A figure documents undigested millet seeds in a veterinary digestive-impaction case. No culinary human exposure or Parkinson symptom outcome is measured.
The original article used C60 in grapeseed oil as a laboratory comparator. It provides no human oral pain outcome, oil grade or shared trial lot.
